source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Sterling campus holds 44 MW of IT capacity across 420,000 square feet, the 12th largest of the 25 Virginia data centers that publish power figures.

Virginia has 330 mapped data center facilities, but only 25 disclose power. Those 25 account for 1,603 MW of announced IT load, and Sterling's 44 MW is 2.7% of it. The published capacity in the state is therefore a small, self-selected slice of the total footprint, and Sterling sits in the middle of that slice rather than at its top.

For AI, the binding number is power delivered to racks. At a training density of 40 kW per rack, 44 MW implies roughly 1,100 racks of compute. The data does not say what density is actually deployed, whether the power is fully utilized, or whether any tenant runs AI workloads at all.

The certifications cover financial services, healthcare, federal compliance, information security, and physical plant standards. They describe what the buildings are qualified to host, not what they host. Tenant mix, utilization, and expansion plans are absent, and the suitability score of 70 is derived only from published IT capacity and operator type, with announced expansion listed as missing. The record establishes size and compliance posture, not AI relevance.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
